metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 3–7% for the next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model fails to react quickly; increase forecast slope by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility, add 1–3% upward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often lags; forecast should be 1–2% higher than actual for the first 3–5 days of positive sentiment.
- If model forecast is flat or declining while sentiment is positive, increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- In absence of clear sentiment signal, model tends to over-smooth; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
